thread:
Jordan K.: Heads-up: third-party integrator reported accidental upload of a config archive containing OAuth client secrets for a few internal apps. They rotated their copy but asked us to rotate ours as precaution.

Jordan K.: Affected scopes we saw in the archive: `svc-deploy`, `metrics-ingest`, `integrations-webhook`. Likely limited to service clients created 2024-2025.

Priya S.: Ugh. Do we have confirmed exposure or just reported?

Jordan K.: We have proof-of-possession screenshots. No indicators of unauthorized access in logs yet, but we should treat as high-risk and rotate.

Nina R.: Proposed immediate actions:
- Rotate client secrets for affected apps.
- Force reissue of tokens (invalidate active sessions).
- Patch CI to stop printing secrets to artifact bundles.
- Notify CS for customers using these integrations.

Sam V.: I'll coordinate infra-side rotations. Quick question: are these OAuth clients used in Dedicated customer installs (private keys stored on their side)?

Jordan K.: Only internal-managed clients. Private/on-prem customers not impacted.

infra-ops: Starting automated secret-rotation job for app group `svc-*` (job id: R-rot-2026-03-23-01). Will rotate in batches of 8 apps/min to avoid bursting token churn.

security-bot: Risk classification: HIGH. Ticket filed -> SEC-1249. Vulnerability window estimated: 0-72h depending on rotation.

Priya S.: Timeline for rotation complete? We need to draft customer messaging if any external partners will experience disruptions.

Sam V.: ETA for rotation job: 2 hours to complete bulk rotation. Will follow with token invalidation wave. Will mark maintenance window in deploy calendar.

Nina R.: CI fix: temporarily block any pipeline that produces `*.tar.gz` artifacts with `secrets/` or `configs/` paths. Patch merged to CI tomorrow morning. In meantime, scanning job will delete any artifact that matches pattern.

Jordan K.: Commands for manual rotation if needed (internal runbook link: https://internal.redwood/sec/rotations/SEC-1249):
```
# list clients
redwood-admin oauth clients list --filter "created:2024-01..2025-12" --output json | jq '.[] | select(.name|test("svc-"))'
# rotate client secret
redwood-admin oauth clients rotate-secret --client-id <id> --reason "sec-1249 third-party leak"
# revoke tokens
redwood-admin oauth tokens revoke --client-id <id> --all
```

Priya S.: I'll prep a short external notice for any downstream partners (if rotation causes 401s) and a CS playbook for handling partner restores.

Sam V.: Rollout note: we'll do zero-downtime rotations for most services by updating clients then gradually restarting dependent pods with backoff. For any critical real-time flows, we'll hold rotation until we coordinate with owners.

Nina R.: Also adding monitoring alert: spike in 401s on webhook endpoints will trigger paging to eng-oncall.

infra-ops: Rotation job finished for first batch (apps 1-120). No 401 spike observed. Continuing.

security-bot: Rotation progress -> 480/480 clients rotated. All secrets rotated and previous secrets revoked. Post-rotation audit started.

Jordan K.: Thanks team. Next steps: audit logs for suspicious token use (48h lookback), update CI guards, and add secret scanning to artifact pipeline. Priya, please coordinate partner comms if we see any downstream errors.

Priya S.: Will do. Draft ready and will post to #customer-success with instructions for reconnect if needed.

Sam V.: Closing SEC-1249 once audit clean. If anyone sees persistent 401s after rotation, ping infra-ops and we'll roll back the client change for that app until we patch the consumer.

Nina R.: Created follow-up ticket to add secret scanner to artifact retention policy. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
